UNIT.sep: Trace mechanisms,link structure to function,control an investigation and distinguish observed evidence from supplied data.
UNIT.careers: Illustrative food-laboratory and biological modelling practices;no clinical diagnosis,nutrition prescription or occupational qualification.
UNIT.focus: Human chemical/mechanical digestion,organ adaptations and controlled qualitative food tests with honest practical/digital evidence.
UNIT.phenomenon: A fictional food report claims a negative sugar test means no carbohydrate and routes food through the pancreas;both conclusions need checking.
UNIT.supportingPhenomena: Food/secretion flow models,enzyme pathways,villus explanations,positive/negative controls and a failed lipid blank.
UNIT.drivingQuestion: How do digestive structures and controlled tests support claims about food? KICD: How is the human digestive system adapted to its functions?
UNIT.storylineThread: Tube and secretions → starch → protein → fat/absorption → controlled-test plan → starch → reducing sugar → protein → cold lipid demonstration → model → digital claim → audit → independent explanation.
UNIT.coreCompetencies:
Digital literacy: as the learner retrieves and saves information from non-print sources on the enzymes used to break down each type of food at different regions of the digestive system and shares the information with peers using digital presentation modes.
Creativity and Imagination: as the learner uses locally available materials to make a model of the human digestive system.
UNIT.values:
Respect: as the learner considers others’ opinions while discussing the adaptations of the human digestive system.
Unity: as the learner works harmoniously when carrying out experiments on food tests.
UNIT.pcis: Safety and security: as the learner observes safety precautions as they carry out experiments on food tests.
UNIT.content: Chemical and mechanical digestion of foods; Adaptations of parts of the human digestive system,; Food tests
UNIT.subject: General Science
UNIT.learningOutcomes:
describe the digestion of different types of food in each region of the digestive system,
explain the adaptations of parts of the human digestive system,
perform experiments to determine presence of different nutrients in food,
appreciate the role played by different parts of the digestive system.

FINAL_EXPLANATION.instructions: Lesson13,40minutes:4procedure,16sections1–2,12section3,4section4,4checking/collection. Work independently with DG12 only. No reagents,teaching cards,models,hints or peer discussion. Supplied data are fictional;do not present them as your own experimental observations. This written final does not certify outcome c's performed experiment or digital/model actions;teacher uses separately observed lesson evidence for those.

sections.title: 1. Route and mechanisms
sections.prompt: Draw a labelled flow model for the DG12 mixed meal through mouth,oesophagus,stomach,small intestine,large intestine,rectum and anus. Add accessory secretion arrows from salivary glands,liver/gallbladder and pancreas. Explain mechanical versus chemical digestion,and trace one starch,protein and fat pathway with relevant sites. Explain why food does not enter pancreas and why bile is not an enzyme.
sections.exemplar: Food follows the alimentary tube;secretions join it. Chewing/mixing alters physical form;enzymes hydrolyse molecules. Starch digestion begins with salivary amylase and continues via pancreatic/intestinal enzymes to absorbable sugars. Stomach protease begins protein breakdown;intestinal proteases/peptidases complete amino acids. Bile from liver/gallbladder disperses fat;pancreatic lipase breaks fat molecules into absorbable products. Food itself does not pass through pancreas. Accept pharynx/duodenum and additional correctly placed detail.

sections.title: 2. Adaptation and absorption
sections.prompt: Explain how two small-intestine adaptations support absorption,including a blood/lymph distinction. Explain one stomach adaptation and its function. Distinguish absorption from assimilation and correct the claim that all water absorption happens in colon.
sections.exemplar: Villi/microvilli provide large area;thin lining shortens crossing distance;blood capillaries/lacteals transport absorbed materials away. Simple sugars/amino acids mainly enter blood;much lipid enters lymph via lacteals. Stomach muscles mix food or protective lining reduces damage;accept a correctly explained adaptation. Absorption crosses gut lining;assimilation uses absorbed material in cells. Both small and large intestines absorb water.

sections.title: 3. Controlled food-test claims
sections.prompt: For DG12 sample X,state a justified conclusion for each of its three tests and explain why a negative Benedict result cannot establish no carbohydrate/no sugar. For Y,decide whether lipid can be concluded and justify a repeat/change. Describe one contamination control and one safety precaution relevant to these tests. State whether interpreting this fictional record proves you performed an experiment.
sections.exemplar: Xstarch detected and protein detected with functioning controls;no reducing sugar detected under stated conditions. This does not exclude non-reducing sugars,other carbohydrates or concentrations below detection. Ylipid inference is invalid because the process blank is milky;repeat with clean apparatus/clear blank and positive control. Separate fresh portions/clean droppers reduce contamination. Accept specific valid safety action such as eye protection,teacher-managed hot bath or ethanol separated from heat/flames. Interpretation alone does not prove practical performance.

sections.title: 4. Organ contribution and evidence limit
sections.prompt: Choose one organ and explain a specific way it contributes to the digestion/absorption of the meal. State a limitation of your drawn model and name one separate observation a teacher would need to confirm your practical or digital skill.
sections.exemplar: For example pancreas supplies enzymes/bicarbonate to the small intestine,or small intestine supports digestion/absorption;accept another accurate organ-role benefit. Drawn arrows cannot demonstrate actual peristalsis,hydrolysis or uptake. Teacher must observe a specified real action such as safe sample labelling/dispensing/recording with controls,or retrieving/saving/sharing a source claim. A written value statement does not establish lasting appreciation.
